children: Aanya Thakur Mumbai: Weak tea demand and rising commodity costs are putting pressure on Tata Consumer Products' core business, prompting the company to lean on salt and newer businesses to sustain growth. Tea volumes remained flat in the September quarter, while unusually hot weather hurt its UK business, even as the consumer goods maker reported double-digit growth in revenue and profit.

The company's consolidated revenue from operations rose 14% to 5,661 crore in the quarter, while the net profit grew 16% to 470 crore. Its Ebitda grew 18% to 794 crore in the period. India tea and coffee revenue declined 1% year-on-year to 1,244 crore, with flat volumes amid weak category demand.

However, this decline comes amid weak industry performance, with overall volumes down about 6%. "The overall industry has been soft. If I look at overall third-party numbers, it's about negative six," company chief Sunil D'Souza told investors on Monday. The company has raised tea prices by around 8-10% between the June quarter and now to offset input cost inflation.

According to D'Souza, the increases had largely covered the inflation seen so far, but their full impact was yet to flow through the numbers. He also flagged the buying cycle after the festive season as a factor to watch. Commodity inflation also weighed on the India business where margins narrowed to 11.1% from 11.5% a year earlier, despite revenue rising 17% to 3,666 crore. Chief financial officer Ashish Goenka attributed this contraction largely to inflation in salt, adding that calibrated price increases had already been taken.

Salt, meanwhile, is closing the gap with tea and coffee. Its revenue rose 15% to 1,099 crore, supported by 9% volume growth, while value-added and premium salt volumes grew 17%. TCPL has also raised prices of its standard orange salt pack from 30 to 32 in May, and to 34 on October 1, after the quarter ended. "We continue to guide salt for mid-single-digit volume," D'Souza said.

International revenue rose 7% to 1,256 crore but fell 2% in constant currency against a high base. In the UK, revenue fell 8% in constant currency as a prolonged heatwave hurt tea consumption. However, the company said it remains positive on a rebound in the region as weather-related challenges ease. "The good news is that the weather has turned, and I do think the UK is going to come back strongly because the share continued to hold out," he said. Its overall international business margins expanded to 13.3% from 11.5%.

title: Tata Consumer Q2 Net Up Despite High Input Cost, Weak Tea Demand
